overview: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, said hackers took about $6.3 billion in digital assets, which analysts and some outlets attribute to North Korea, and the company said it will cover the losses. Midterm elections are two days away, and news organizations are explaining how they will call races. Youth-led protests have spread from France to other European countries, and Poland's president and government are in a court dispute. Oil companies reported another quarter of large profits as the war involving Iran keeps crude prices high.

markets.summary: The latest readings show US stocks mixed: the S&P 500 rose 0.28% on its last reading (Oct. 28), while the Nasdaq fell 1.38% and the Dow 1.09% on later days, and Japan's Nikkei dropped 2.12%. Bluesky chatter pointed to tech stocks falling after earnings, though the data here doesn't confirm a single cause. Oil remains very high, with Brent near $123 a barrel and WTI up about 21% in a month, which news reports tie to the Middle East conflict; OPEC+ delegates told Reuters and Bloomberg the group will keep its December output targets unchanged. Treasury yields eased (the 10-year fell 7 basis points to 4.98%), but the 30-year mortgage rate is still 7.24%. Inflation ran at 3.72% in September, up from the prior month. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point.

Dropped 2.12% and is down about 5% over a month; no cause is clear from today's coverage.
Inflation rose to 3.72% year over year, up 0.36 percentage points from the previous reading.

concept.explanation: OPEC+ is a group of oil-producing countries, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, that agrees on how much crude each member may pump. Fewer barrels on the market tends to push prices up, and more tends to push them down. Because crude is the main input for gasoline and diesel, the group's decisions can show up at the pump and in shipping and airline costs within weeks. Delegates say the group will hold December targets steady.

watch: OPEC+ is expected to confirm unchanged December oil output targets, per delegates (date not yet confirmed)
